newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka president to pay surprise visit to India.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka president to pay surprise visit to India.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga was expected in New Delhi on Tuesday for a week-long private visit but officials said she would also hold talks with Indian leaders on her country's ethnic war.

Indian newspapers said Kumaratunga's surprise visit follows reports of an offer by the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) to hold peace talks with her government through unidentified mediators.
"The president is expected here on a private visit, but she will also meet Indian leaders for informal talks," an Indian official told Reuters.
An official source had earlier suggested the president might have already arrived, but the official denied that.
A Sri Lankan official said his embassy would "make a statement on this matter later", but declined to say more. "We cannot comment on this for security reasons," another Sri Lankan official said.
The Indian Express newspaper said: "Amid reports of impending negotiations with the LTTE through mediators President Kumaratunga leaves for New Delhi on Tuesday."
A former Indian diplomat to Sri Lanka said Kumaratunga was due to arrive with her two children.
"My information is that she had planned to take a holiday from the pressures of the civil war in her country," he told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
"Of course she will use the occasion to hold informal talks in New Delhi. But nothing more than that should be seen in this visit," he said.

The Hindu newspaper said Sri Lankan Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar who had arrived in India for a ministerial meeting of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) last week was still in New Delhi.
There was, however, no independent confirmation of Kadirgamar's presence in New Delhi.

India has been closely involved in Sri Lanka's turbulent ethnic crises, providing armed assistance to Colombo in fending off a hardline Sinhalese-led rebellion and later by sending in troops there in a failed attempt to disarm the LTTE.
Tens of thousands of Indian troops were sent to Sri Lanka following a pact between the two governments in 1987.

They were subsequently ordered out of the island nation in 1990 after Colombo began talks with LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran. India's involvement was severely criticised by opposition groups in New Delhi as a "misadventure".
Kumaratunga last visited India for a SAARC summit in May last year.
But she had to cut short her stay at that time after the LTTE shot down an air force plane, signalling a resumption of its 13-year old war against Colombo following a brief truce.
